answer.reason: In EIA state electricity profiles, Table 1 breaks down net generation by producer type. New Hampshire's total net generation is dominated by independent power producers—most notably the Seabrook nuclear station—which account for the bulk of the state's roughly 17 million MWh. Traditional electric utilities in New Hampshire own very little generation capacity, so their reported net generation is only on the order of a few thousand megawatthours (6,888 MWh), not the ~16.9 million MWh figure, which corresponds to the independent power producer (and combined total) categories. Therefore, the value listed for Electric utilities is 6,888 megawatthours.
